content: HIV infection requires strict adherence to prescribed medications to reduce the risk of transmission to others. It is essential to take all HIV medications exactly as directed by your healthcare provider. During sexual activity, use effective barrier methods such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams as instructed by your doctor. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Before starting darunavir or refilling your prescription, read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, carefully follow the Instructions for Use included with the product. Take darunavir orally with food as directed by your doctor. It must be taken at the same time as certain other medications, typically once or twice daily. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose accurately using a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is determined based on your age, lab tests, medical condition, and response to treatment. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not stop taking it or other HIV medications without your doctor’s approval, even for a short time. Darunavir is always taken with other HIV medications, making it challenging to identify which drug may be causing side effects. However, darunavir is known to cause diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and headaches. This medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune system may lead to symptoms at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Rarely, darunavir may increase blood sugar levels, potentially causing or worsening diabetes. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. If you already have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. This medication may also rarely cause severe, potentially fatal liver problems. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking darunavir, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. A serious allergic reaction to darunavir is rare, but it can commonly cause a rash, which is usually not severe. However, it may be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for guidance. Before taking darunavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Darunavir passes into breast milk, so discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Darunavir can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of darunavir from your body, altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, garlic supplements, certain rifamycins (rifampin, rifapentine), and St. John’s wort. Darunavir may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In case of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (e.g., liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, blood sugar) should be conducted. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose and are taking this medication twice daily, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than six hours before the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. If you are taking this medication once daily and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours before the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid form in its original container and do not refrigerate or freeze it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
